title: Sweep Up — approximate patch and estimated MIDI
method: Long-window FFT and spectrograms separate stable low harmonic families from the rising resonant band. The first three passages support approximate held fifths Eb2/Bb2, Ab2/Eb3, and Db2/Ab2. Higher peaks are mostly integer harmonics and are not automatically turned into extra MIDI notes. Voicing and gates remain assumptions tied to this software patch.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI and recording-specific factory SysEx are unavailable. This is an estimated audio reconstruction, not an exact original performance or authenticated factory patch.
Every note-on velocity is fixed to 100 as an explicit unknown placeholder; note-off velocity is 64. These values were not recovered from the audio.
Played-key octave and voicing are conditional on the newly designed patch. The hardware oscillator tuning, system transpose, original key presses, controller changes, and effect history are unknown.
Onsets refer to the decoded public MP3. MP3 encoder delay, hardware latency, recording processing, exact gates, and release tails are not recovered.

A differently tuned multi-oscillator factory patch could generate these families from fewer or differently pitched keys. The MIDI fifths are a plausible rendering voicing, not recovered physical key presses.
Slow envelopes obscure note-off timing. The final chord is deliberately held to the excerpt boundary; the source recording continues.
The sweep could combine envelope, LFO, and live controls. The software uses a chosen rising filter envelope and gentle LFO, not recovered controller data.

patch_design.name: APX SweepUp
rationale: Two slightly detuned saws reproduce the stable low harmonic families and their beating.
A low starting cutoff with a slow rising resonant envelope approximates the strongly moving spectral emphasis.
Soft amplitude attack, moderate release, and a restrained modulated delay/reverb approximate the continuous background around chord changes.
uncertainties: These are newly designed software parameters informed by the public demo, not recovered Roland factory settings.
No authentic factory dump or controlled hardware measurements exist for this comparison.
The chosen two-note fifths and detuned saw layer are a non-unique explanation of the audio. They do not establish the factory oscillator tuning or true key count.
